scenes.narration: A stranger in your DMs says he works for wallet support. He wants you to verify your wallet. Badger already hates this.

Here is how the trick works. The scammer watches public help channels. When you ask a question in public, he messages you first, acts friendly, and sends a link to a fake verification page. [src:ftc-crypto-scams]

onScreen.title: How the fake support trick works
bullets: They send a fake verification link

scenes.narration: Badger's Red Flag: a countdown. The page says your wallet will be frozen in {10|ten} minutes unless you type your recovery phrase. Real support never asks for it. [src:ftc-crypto-scams]
Zoo's One Fix. Only use support links from the official website, never from a direct message. Never type your recovery phrase into any page. And if you lost money, report it. [src:ftc-report]

onScreen.title: Zoo's One Fix
steps: Use support links from the official website only
Never type your recovery phrase into a page
Report the account, then block it

scenes.narration: If this saved you a bad afternoon, subscribe. Badger will keep judging the links, so you don't have to.
